acceptance_basis.directive_interpretation: Codex is the acceptance authority under the owner directive for the autonomous Forteca program. This receipt is controller acceptance, not an AICG PASS claim.

root_cause_or_implementation_gap: The trash state was not a real list boundary: the loader returned only active leads, archived metadata was not requested, restore used native confirmation, and the reference action ownership was hidden behind generic page-header suppression. FRT-009 now requests the real archived-capable list, excludes active records from trash, derives filters and metadata from returned records, routes restore through the existing update mutation and ConfirmDialog, and exposes only real trash actions.

rules: Trash membership is derived from canonical archive/soft-delete/outcome fields returned by the real list response; no screenshot row, count, name, owner or date is hardcoded.
Retention dates, deleted-by values, restore audit counts and deletion reasons are shown only when persisted in the record; unavailable values are stated rather than invented.
The reference controls, hierarchy, density and table intent are reconciled without reproducing unsupported 30-day policy or irreversible bulk deletion behavior.
Restore remains owned by the existing lead update mutation and shared ConfirmDialog; no parallel delete/restore data model is introduced.
Every visible trash control is backed by a real query, derived filter, export handler, route toggle, pagination owner or existing mutation; dead screenshot-only controls are not accepted.

visible_controls_wired: The visible export, active-view toggle, search, trash filters, summary reset, pagination and row restore path use real runtime data or existing owners. The current real response has zero archived rows, so no Restore button is fabricated into the empty table.
